Analysis by Richard Cowan

The reaction to the statement by Rev. Jeremiah Wright regarding the origins of AIDS is a major indication of how badly our democracy is functioning. It was never really discussed in any meaningful way. 

Wright claims, “The government lied about inventing the HIV virus as a means of genocide against people of color.” I think that the idea is absurd, but it is still important to address this question, because his views are very widely shared in the African American community and elsewhere. 

For an excellent discussion of this problem,

see

Rev. Wright and PEPFAR, AIDS Complicity by Scott Swenson, RH Reality Check on March 21, 2008 

Swenson says, “Legitimate scientists and public health experts counter every argument at AIDS Truth.org. If you have doubts, please visit that site.” 

It is important to understand that even if the conspiracy theory were valid, it would tell us nothing about how we should deal with the reality of the present situation. If it was intended to be a race-specific pathogen, something clearly went terribly wrong. However, this is not to say that deliberate government policies in the US, Africa, and most of the rest of the world have made the situation much worse. Most of these issues are “off-topic” for MarijuanaNews.com, but one that is never mentioned is very much a part of our world. 

Sadly, no one in either the AIDS establishment or the African American leadership will address the issue of medical cannabis as the most practical way of helping the most people in 

Africa who have AIDS and many other diseases. 

See 

On World AIDS Day Medical Cannabis Is Not Just A Forbidden Medicine, It is A Forbidden Topic. 

Now let’s quickly review the key points in the issue. The scale of the problem is huge.

“Sub-Saharan Africa is more heavily affected by HIV and AIDS than any other region of the world. An estimated 22.5 million people were living with HIV at the end of 2007 and approximately 1.7 million additional people were infected with HIV during that year. In just the past year, the AIDS epidemic in Africa has claimed the lives of an estimated 1.6 million people in this region. More than eleven million children have been orphaned by AIDS.” (By comparison, “only” 200,000 people have died as a result of the genocide in Darfur, and “only” 700,000 were killed in the Rwandan genocide.) 

Wikipedia has an excellent overview of the problem, and points out that “Anti-Retro-Viral patients need regular testing of viral load and CD4 cell count. This requires expensive laboratory equipment and good healthcare logistics. These costs drive the price of generic ARV therapy in African countries up from under $140 USD pppy for the drugs alone to approximately $800 USD pppy when done according to Western standards.For many Africans, living below the poverty threshold of a $2 USD / day, free (government or NGO-funded) treatment remains the only option.” 

In other words, most people with AIDS in Africa are unlikely to be able to afford any modern medicines. Moreover, many of those who do get ARV treatment are going to suffer from nausea, as is the case in the US and other developed countries. The prevalence of this problem is evidenced by the fact that the FDA has approved Marinol, synthetic THC, for the treatment of AIDS/ARV related nausea. 

See 

Marinol Was The First Schedule 2 Drug To Be "Down-Scheduled," 

Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site. 

Doesn’t That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway?

and links, especially, see 

A Medical Marijuana User Says That "Marinol Rescheduling Is Worthless" For Him.He Simply Cannot Afford It. "My country is killing me." 

The fact is that Marinol is much too expensive even for most people in the US, and whole cannabis is preferred by most patients, even if they can afford Marinol, which very few Africans can. It is also worth noting that for AIDS in Africa was known as the “Slim disease”, because the patients simply wasted away, having lost all appetite. The point is that the argument widely used by Western prohibitionists, that Medical cannabis is not necessary because we now have pharmaceuticals that meet the needs of patients, is irrelevant in Africa, even if it were true in the US. Therefore, by the US government’s own standards, there is a need for medical cannabis in Africa which can only be met by allowing the medical use of whole cannabis.

 

However, these countries also lack the medical/legal infrastructure to provide the equivalent of the US and Canadian “medical marijuana” exemptions to cannabis prohibition. It would be absurd to tell impoverished Africans with AIDS that they should see a doctor and get a letter that would allow them to grow their own. Moreover, so long as cannabis is contraband in their countries they would have the same problems faced by patients in states with medical marijuana laws. They are not going to be able to grow indoors, so their plants would be valuable and very vulnerable to theft.

 

Consequently, only by making cannabis fully legal, and therefore not valuable enough to steal, will poor people be able to afford it. 

What can the US do? 

First, it can get out of the way, or to quote the Hippocratic Oath, “First do no harm.” The fact is that the US Drug War is the major impediment to allowing these countries to legalize cannabis. 

However, at this point that would not be nearly enough. Unless the US actively pushes a realistic plan for cannabis in these countries, it is not going to happen. 

First, only the US has the influence to get the UN out of the way. Sadly, the organization that is supposed to protect the sovereignty of these countries has become an instrument of their subjugation to the Drug War. These programs have taken on a life of their own and only the US can stop them. 

See 

The UN Commission on Narcotic Drugs Resolution on the Control of Cannabis in Africa. UN Narks Urge War on Poorest of the Poor. Cannabis Prohibition Does Most Damage In Poor Countries. 

and 

UN Agency Tries to Get Swazis To Switch From Insangu To Hemp Cultivation. Weird, And Sad, But Interesting. 

and 

Is The UN An Instrument of Peace and Freedom Or Of War and Tyranny? UN Narks Make Answer Clear. Lies and Hatred In Service To International Police State. (International Narcotics Control Board Report) 

However, while getting the UN out of the way is necessary, it will not be sufficient. The problem is that after all these years of pseudo-scientific prohibitionist propaganda, these countries’ own medical establishments are as filled with quackery as those in the West. See 

Chewing and Injecting Marijuana A Major Health Problem In Uganda? Or Quackery, and Corruption? How Reefer Madness Kills the Most Vulnerable. Selective Indignation, Indeed. 

The US spends billions of dollars every year on fighting AIDS in Africa under a program called PEPFAR (President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief). If the US were to incorporate cannabis into this program and insist that the recipient countries make cannabis available to their citizens, they would have to listen and cooperate. Fortunately, there is plenty of useful information available regarding the value of cannabis to people with AIDS, despite the best/worst efforts of the US government.

See 

People With AIDS Benefit From – Not Harmed by Medical Marijuana in Government Approved Test. Politically Very Important – Medically Pointless. 

This information could be used to educate the public health officials of the various African countries. If any of these countries could be persuaded to end the prohibition of cannabis, the benefit to their citizens would be obvious within a year or so and the rest of the countries could follow suit. 

Unfortunately, there remains the problem of the context of the international Drug War. While the US is the primary force behind prohibitionism, it is by no means the only source of its support. 

First, prohibitionism is an international ideology that is useful to authoritarian governments everywhere. 

See 

Science, Democracy, Ideology and the Prohibitionist Police State. Marijuana Use Doesn’t Hurt “Thinking Skills” But Prohibition Does. Analysis by Richard Cowan

and 

New Dutch Study on "Licit and illicit drug use in the Netherlands" Shows Why International Anti-Dutch Prohibitionist Propaganda Campaign Is Vital to Drug Warriors. How Ideology Works. 

Second, people with AIDS in Africa cannot wait until the Drug War has ended, and increasingly Sub-Saharan Africa has become a transit route for cocaine and other hard drugs being smuggled into Europe. 

See 

The Drug War Is Politics By Other Means: Blackwater Gets Billions to Fight “Narco-Terorism”. Buying Constituencies for the Drug War. Analysis by Richard Cowan 

Bluntly, many of the countries in Sub-Saharan Africa are authoritarian kleptocracies and the Drug War is a major source of graft and police power, a problem not unknown in the US. 

See 

The Invisible Context: The Drug War Is the Context for Marijuana Prohibition, But It Is Also The Context for Everything Else. 

Consequently, it is only realistic to recognize that the legalization of cannabis will have to take place within the context of the Drug War. The police and the local quacks can shift their focus to drugs that really are dangerous and use their very limited resources to go after gangs who use their countries as entrepots. 

Also, these countries could maintain bans on the export of cannabis, which would placate the prohibitionists and have the added benefit of lowering the value of the plants, further reducing the risk of their being stolen from patients and growers. 

Of course, everything that has been said here also applies to most of the rest of the world, especially to Mexico, and its problems with the US Drug War are even ore serious because it is out neighbor. 

See 

More Progress In The Netherlands; More Violence In Mexico. Lawless Law Enforcement in San Diego. Police “Robbing” the Medical Cannabis Deliveries? 

Do I expect any such triumph of decency to happen soon? No, of course not! 

However, the next time you hear someone demanding that we “do something” about Darfur, remind them that AIDS is killing far more people in Africa, and we Americans are responsible for these deaths in a way that we are not responsible for the tragedy in Darfur. We have learned the hard way over the last few years that there are many problems we cannot solve, but there also plenty that we can stop making worse.

Afterward: 

From time to time I have written that the suppression of medical cannabis is mass murder, but no one seems to take this statement seriously enough even to object to it as an “overstatement.” 

See 

World AIDS Day: More Proof That the Suppression Of Medical Cannabis – Indeed Cannabis Prohibition Itself – Is Mass Murder. Analysis by Richard Cowan

and 

Marijuana Derivative Blocks Irreversible Brain Damage After Accidents; Another Way Marijuana Prohibition Kills 

and 

Patient Who Was Denied Liver Transplant For Using Medical Marijuana Dies -- How Lies Kill -- 2 articles 

That lack of response is typical of our treatment of the cannabis issues, generally. When the annual US marijuana arrest numbers are announced, they are generally ignored.

See 

More Arresting Developments. Record Marijuana Arrests Go Unreported. “No Medicine Is Smoked” – So DEA Busts Edibles Maker. 

When someone is shot dead in a police raid, it may be reported, but never in a way that gives any idea of the extent of the violence. 

See 

What Is the Real Strategy Behind the Czar’s “Strategy ”? 40,000 SWAT Raids Per Year. One In Nine Young Black Males (20 To 34) Are Locked Up. 

When there is a proposal to stop arresting sick and dying people for using cannabis, no one objects when law enforcement opposes it claiming medical expertise. 

See 

Learning About Prohibitionism: House Debate on Medical Marijuana Bill Offers New Insight Into Police State Ideology. 

and 

Reading Between The Lies. New Version of An Old Lie About My Saying Medical Cannabis Is A “Scam” May Be Clue to New Prohibitionist Party Line. Only A Few Hundred Patients? 

and 

California Narks Lie to Justify Disobeying Prop 215. And They Lie About Me In The Process. 

and finally, 

The People Behind The Medical Marijuana Conspiracy October 28, 1998
